newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa rests after leaving hospital.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa rests after leaving hospital.

text.p: Mother Teresa was released from hospital on Friday after a battle with heart problems, malaria and pneumonia, and immediately went home to rest.

Doctors said the 86-year-old Nobel peace laureate, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her work with the destitute, was released from Calcutta's Woodland's Nursing Home at her own request early on Friday.
The Roman Catholic nun was taken by wheelchair, ambulance and stretcher to her nearby home from the hospital, which she entered on August 20 with malaria.
Doctors said Mother Teresa, fitted with a heart pacemaker since 1989, suffered two heart attacks while in intensive care in the hospital and also had a bout of mild pneumonia.

"We had a plan to release her on Saturday but she was restless and wanted to go home today. We could not force her to stay one more day," Dr S.K. Sen, the nursing home's medical director, told reporters.
"She is a little stronger but she needs lots of rest," he said.

One sister at the Mother House, Mother Teresa's home and the headquarters of her Calcutta-based Missionaries of Charity religious order, told reporters: "Mother is very happy to return home. God has listened to our prayers.
"She is now on her bed and resting as per the advice of the doctors... We will have special prayers throughout the day," she told reporters.
Sen said: "She has tremendous power. She becomes stronger after every prayer."
Leaving the hospital, Mother Teresa thanked doctors for all they had done for her. "May God bless you," she said.
Mother Teresa's stay in hospital attracted international attention as members of Missionaries of Charity held round-the-clock prayers for her recovery.
Her room at the Mother House has been equipped with artificial respiratory equipment, doctors said.
Mother Teresa has spent much of her life surrounded by the sick, the destitute and the dying.
The Missionaries of Charity, which she founded in 1949, runs some 544 homes for unwanted children and the destitute in more than 80 cities.
The work includes the care of nearly 7,000 children in 120 homes and arranging 1,500 adoptions each year.
In 1991, Mother Teresa was treated at a Californian hospital for heart disease and bacterial pneumonia.
Two years later, she fell in Rome and broke three ribs. In August 1993, she developed malaria, complicated by her heart and lung problems. Last April, she fractured her left collar bone.
Mother Teresa was born Agnes Goinxha Bejaxhiu to Albanian parents in Skopje, in what was then Serbia, on August 27, 1910.
